ਮੇਰਾ ਗੁਰੁ ਪਰਮੇਸਰੁ ਸੁਖਦਾਈ ॥:
A personal confession of faith: the Guru is the embodied form of the Transcendent Lord, the giver of every comfort and lasting peace. It is an intimate affirmation of refuge and trust, equating the spiritual guide with the divine presence that removes suffering and bestows serenity.  
Themes: Guru as divine embodiment, Transcendent Lord, giver of peace, source of all comfort, refuge, trust, removal of suffering, serenity
ਤੁਮ ਦਾਤੇ ਤੁਮ ਪੁਰਖ ਬਿਧਾਤੇ ॥:
You are the sole Giver and the all-pervading Architect who fashions every destiny. Direct address of praise and trust, acknowledging the Divine as origin, sustainer, and bestower of every gift to all beings. Creation, provision, and fate rest entirely in divine hands.  
Themes: divine generosity, divine sovereignty, creation, providence, destiny, all-pervasiveness, trust, praise
ਕਰੁਣਾ ਮੈ ਕਿਰਪਾਲ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਨਿਧਿ ਜੀਵਨ ਪਦ ਨਾਨਕ:
Addressing the Divine as compassion embodied, the source and storehouse of mercy, the speaker pleads for the gift of darshan (vision of the Divine presence). This sight is sought as transformative grace that elevates the soul into true spiritual life, granting the rank of redeemed, God-centred existence while still alive.  
Themes: divine mercy, compassionate grace, darshan/blessed vision, longing for God, spiritual transformation, living liberation, refuge.
ਤੂੰ ਭਾਰੋ ਠਾਕੁਰੁ ਗੁਣੀ ਗਹੇਰਾ ॥੨॥:
Direct address praising the Divine as the supreme Lord and Master, weighty with authority and deep of heart. The heaviness conveys sovereign greatness; the depth conveys an unfathomable inner nature. The speaker declares that every virtue resides fully in God, affirming divine majesty and moral completeness. This is reverent acknowledgment of overwhelming divine greatness, not a petition.

Themes: divine sovereignty, praise of the Divine, fullness of virtue, depth of divine nature, reverent acknowledgment, divine majesty, moral completeness
ਦੇਵਣਹਾਰੁ ਦਾਤਾਰੁ ਕਿਤੁ ਮੁਖਿ ਸਾਲਾਹੀਐ ॥:
The divine is the Giver (Dataar) and generous Lord who endlessly provides sustenance to all living beings, and this overwhelming generosity reduces the speaker to wondering what mouth could possibly praise it adequately. It is a confession of human inadequacy: no finite tongue can fully extol the infinite Giver.  
Themes: divine generosity, the Giver, human inadequacy, limits of speech, humility before the infinite, praise, provision, wonder
ਤੇਰੇ ਕਵਨ ਕਵਨ ਗੁਣ ਕਹਿ ਕਹਿ ਗਾਵਾ ਤੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਗ:
Overwhelmed by limitless divine qualities, the speaker asks which of them could possibly be sung, since no enumeration can exhaust them. The question is itself an act of praise, marveling at the Lord as Master and inexhaustible treasure-house of all excellence and sustaining power.

Themes: infinite divine virtues, praise through wonder, divine sovereignty, inexhaustible treasure, devotional singing, human inadequacy before divine greatness
ਰੇ ਬਉਰੇ ਤੁਹਿ ਘਰੀ ਨ ਰਾਖੈ ਕੋਈ ॥:
Addressing the deluded mind as a madman, this is a stark warning that at the final hour no person, family, or household will give refuge or let the soul remain even for an instant. The temporary welcome of worldly relations collapses, exposing the false security of human shelter and urging the madman to abandon dependence on others.

Themes: mortality, impermanence, false security, worldly attachment, death, isolation, homelessness, admonition.
ਕਾਹੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਡੋਲਤਾ ਹਰਿ ਮਨਸਾ ਪੂਰਣਹਾਰੁ ॥:
Admonishing the restless mind, the speaker asks why it wavers in anxiety when the Divine is the fulfiller of every hope and desire. Wavering embodies doubt and unstable trust; the utterance corrects and steadies the mind, redirecting it from fear to assured reliance on divine providence.  
Themes: restless mind, self-admonition, doubt and anxiety, trust in divine provision, God as fulfiller of desires, inner stability, faith over wavering.
ਰੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਭੀ ਭਜੁ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ॥੨॥:
The speaker turns inward and commands the restless mind to devote itself to Gobind, the Lord of the Universe, through loving remembrance and praise. The tone is urgent self-admonition: the mind must not remain idle or distracted but must personally take up simran (loving remembrance) and vibrate with the divine Name.  
Themes: self-admonition, mind, Gobind, loving remembrance, simran, devotional urgency, personal effort, divine praise.
ਮਨ ਮੇਰਿਆ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਤੇਰੈ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਵਸਤੁ:
Addressing the mind, this admonishes that the treasure—the Divine Presence and source of all true contentment—already dwells within, so hunting for it outside in forests or worldly things is futile. It corrects the restless outward gaze and redirects attention inward to the indwelling reality.
Themes: inner divinity, spiritual treasure within, admonishing one's own mind, futility of outward search, divine indwelling, contentment within, inward turning
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਤੂ ਕਾਏ ਦੇਖਿ ਭੁਲਾਨਾ ॥:
An urgent rebuke to the deluded mind: seeing only the glitter of maya (worldly attachment), it has lost its way and abandoned the path of spiritual life. The speaker calls the listener a madman for mistaking transient sights for reality and commands attention before the error becomes ruin.  
Themes: delusion, maya, worldly attachment, spiritual blindness, admonishing the mind, losing the life-path, discernment
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਥੀਉ ਰੇਣੁ ਜਿਨੀ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਧਿਆਇਆ ॥:
An urgent self-admonition addressed to the mind as a madman: become the dust beneath the feet of those who practice simran (loving remembrance) of the Divine. The image of dust is both abject humility and a prescription — effacing the ego and serving the God-remembering ones is the only way to attain union with the Divine.

Themes: humility, dust of the saints' feet, self-effacement, simran (loving remembrance), surrender, service to the devout, union with the Divine, ego-dissolution.
ਲਖ ਖੁਸੀਆ ਪਾਤਿਸਾਹੀਆ ਜੇ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਨਦਰਿ ਕਰੇਇ:
The True Guru’s single merciful glance outweighs a hundred thousand royal pleasures. Sovereignty and worldly luxury are nothing compared to the inner wealth received through that grace. The statement exalts spiritual blessing over earthly kingship, declaring the Guru’s kind attention the greatest happiness and fulfillment.

Themes: Guru's grace, divine glance, spiritual wealth over worldly sovereignty, royal pleasures, contentment, blessing, inner fulfillment
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ ਤਾ ਦੁਖੁ ਨ ਜਾਣੀਐ ॥:
The merciful True Guru embodies divine compassion: when this grace descends, affliction ceases to be felt as affliction, and the mind no longer recognizes pain as pain. The statement promises that the Guru’s kindness removes suffering by transforming awareness, leaving inner stillness rather than anguish.

Themes: True Guru’s mercy, grace removes suffering, transformed awareness, freedom from pain, divine compassion, inner stillness, refuge in the Guru.
ਹਰਿ ਚਉਥੜੀ ਲਾਵ ਮਨਿ ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਹਰਿ ਪਾਇਆ ਬਲਿ:
The fourth wedding round marks completion: the soul-bride’s restless mind settles into sahaj, effortless inner equipoise, and she realizes the Divine as found within. She exclaims loving surrender—a sacrifice to the Beloved. It declares that union with the Divine and lasting peace are received by grace, not won by effort.

Themes: fourth wedding round, sahaj/equanimity, divine union, soul-bride, surrender, grace, inner peace, finding the Divine
ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਮਨਾਇ ॥:
Enshrining the True Guru in the heart—pleasing him through inner devotion—brings peace and the fulfillment of every desire. A personal testimony of attainment: heartfelt surrender to the Guru’s indwelling presence yields lasting contentment and all desired fruits, not through outward actions but through inner union.

Themes: True Guru, inward enshrinement, peace, spiritual fulfillment, surrender, devotion, contentment, inner presence
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਮੇਰਾ ਸਦਾ ਸਹਾਈ ਜਿਨਿ ਦੁਖ ਕਾ ਕਾਟਿਆ:
Declares personal trust in the True Guru as an ever-present helper and support, tearing down the banner of pain and cutting the very root of suffering for all who seek refuge. It is a testimony of grateful reliance and deliverance from sorrow through the Guru’s protection.  
Themes: True Guru as refuge, ever-present help, removal of suffering, surrender, trust, liberation from pain, protection
ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਮਿਲਣ ਕੀ ਇਹ ਤੇਰੀ ਬਰੀਆ ॥:
The present human birth is your allotted turn for meeting Gobind, the Lord of the Universe. The utterance confronts the soul with urgency: this one opening for divine union must not be postponed. The image of a personal turn makes the chance direct, appointed, and easily lost.
Themes: opportunity, human birth, divine meeting, urgency, purpose of human life, Gobind
ਪ੍ਰਾਣੀ ਤੂੰ ਆਇਆ ਲਾਹਾ ਲੈਣਿ ॥:
A direct address to the human soul, urgently reminding it that birth is a marketplace opportunity: the mortal trader is sent to earn the profit of the divine Name (naam), not worldly goods. Life’s purpose is spiritual gain through remembrance and devotion; the tone is a wake-up call warning against squandering this rare chance.

Themes: purpose of human birth, spiritual profit, divine Name (naam), trade and commerce imagery, urgent admonition, remembrance, opportunity of life, warning against waste
ਹਰਿ ਭਗਤਿ ਦ੍ਰਿੜੁ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਾਧ ਨਾਨਕ ਤੇਰੈ ਕਾਮਿ:
An urgent self-admonition to seek the Guru’s presence and the holy sangat (company of the devout), and to implant devotional worship of the Divine firmly in the heart. Only this steadfast Bhagti (loving devotion) proves useful when all else fails; make it reliable before the end.  
Themes: holy company, Guru’s guidance, heart-implanted devotion, spiritual urgency, final utility, self-admonition
ਜੀਵਨਾ ਸਫਲ ਜੀਵਨ ਸੁਨਿ ਹਰਿ ਜਪਿ ਜਪਿ ਸਦ ਜੀਵਨਾ:
The ear receives the divine Name and the tongue repeats it; through this hearing and chanting a human life becomes fruitful, truly alive, and enduring beyond death. The central declaration equates successful living with constant absorption in naam (the divine Name) and simran (loving remembrance), not with worldly achievement. A worthwhile life is one spent in continual meditation on the Lord.

Themes: fruitful life, hearing the divine Name, chanting and meditation, naam, simran, constant remembrance, spiritual success, eternal life.
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਆਧਾਰੁ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਆਸਰਾ ॥:
The lotus feet of the Divine are the devotee's only foundation, shelter, and steadying anchor. This declares total reliance: the humble servant has no other prop, resting entirely on that sacred presence as life's support, refuge, and ground of stability.  
Themes: lotus feet, divine presence, refuge, surrender, humility, reliance, spiritual anchor, support
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸੇਵੀ ਰਿਦ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਗੁਰ ਪੂਰੇ ਕੈ ਆਧਾਰਿ:
A prayerful aspiration: with the perfect Guru as support, one keeps the Lord’s lotus feet—the Divine presence and refuge—fixed within the heart through inward loving meditation. It is a plea for grace and a resolve to sustain heart-centred devotion.
Themes: lotus feet, divine presence, refuge and surrender, heart-centred meditation, perfect Guru as support, grace, inward devotion
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸਿਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਰੀਤਿ ਸੰਤਨ ਮਨਿ ਆਵਏ ਜੀਉ:
Love for the lotus feet of the Divine—the tender image of refuge at God’s presence—is a settled way of life, and it has come to dwell in the minds of the saints alone. It exalts this loving devotion as an inner discipline and fixed spiritual norm, not a passing feeling, defining the very character of holy persons.

Themes: lotus feet as refuge, divine presence, loving devotion, settled way of life, minds of the saints, inner spiritual discipline, holy character.
ਬੋਹਿਥੜਾ ਹਰਿ ਚਰਣ ਮਨ ਚੜਿ ਲੰਘੀਐ ॥:
The mind is urged: climb aboard the boat of the Lord's lotus feet to cross the ocean of worldly existence. Those feet are the vessel of refuge and grace that carries the soul beyond suffering and transmigration. Surrender at the Divine presence is made concrete as a sea-crossing, and the passage to liberation is assured for those who board.  
Themes: lotus feet, boat/vessel, crossing world-ocean, refuge, surrender, divine grace, liberation, instruction to the mind
ਹਰਿ ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਮਨੁ ਬੇਧਿਆ ਕਿਛੁ ਆਨ ਨ ਮੀਠਾ ਰਾਮ:
The mind is pierced through by the Lord’s lotus feet—tender divine presence and refuge—so no other pleasure tastes sweet. An all-consuming, single-pointed devotion: once simran (loving remembrance) of the Lord King fills awareness, worldly sweetness turns tasteless and God alone remains desirable.

Themes: lotus feet, refuge and surrender, pierced mind, exclusive devotion, divine sweetness, detachment from worldly desire, sovereign Lord King
ਪੀ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਆਘਾਨਿਆ ਗੁਰਿ ਅਮਰੁ ਕਰਾਇਆ ॥੨॥:
Drinking the ambrosial nectar of the divine Name, the soul is filled and fully satisfied; through the Guru it is made immortal, beyond old age, death, and all sorrow. This declares the culminating deathless state conferred by the Guru's grace.

Themes: amrit (divine nectar), naam, immortality, Guru's transforming grace, spiritual contentment, liberation from suffering.
ਜਿਨ੍ਹ ਪੀਆ ਸੇ ਮਸਤ ਭਏ ਹੈ ਤੂਟੇ ਬੰਧਨ ਫਾਹੇ ॥:
Drinking the nectar of naam (the divine Name) brings spiritual intoxication and inner rapture. The drunkenness is liberating absorption, not dullness; the ropes and snares of maya (worldly attachment) snap apart. Declares the transforming outcome of imbibing the divine Name: ecstatic freedom and release from every worldly entanglement.
Themes: naam nectar, divine intoxication, spiritual rapture, release from maya, cutting worldly bonds, liberation, inner absorption, severed shackles
ਹਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਸੋ ਚਖੈ ਮੇਰੇ ਮਨਾ ॥੨॥:
A direct address to the mind holds up the person who drinks the Lord’s amrit, the immortalizing nectar, as truly alive. The nectar is the life-giving water of naam, the divine Name, tasted inwardly. It urges the mind to seek that direct spiritual nourishment and recognize it as the source of real life.  
Themes: amrit (immortalizing nectar), naam (divine Name), inner taste, spiritual life, self-instruction to the mind, divine nourishment, immortality.
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
An urgent instruction to fellow seekers: drink the Lord’s rasa—His essence as nectar—not merely tasting but fully imbibing divine presence as inner sustenance. The teeka directs this through surrender to the perfect Guru and repetition of the divine Name, naam. Drinking conveys both sensory delight and complete absorption; the command turns spiritual life into consuming and being nourished by God.

Themes: divine nectar, drinking/imbibing the Lord’s essence, naam japna (repetition of the divine Name), refuge in the perfect Guru, spiritual sustenance, exhortation to fellow seekers, inner absorption in God.
ਗੁਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਹਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਚੋਇਆ ਮੇਰੀ ਜਿੰਦੁੜੀ:
Addressing the soul intimately, the speaker testifies that the Guru has poured the Lord’s amrit—the immortalising nectar of naam, the divine Name—into her mouth, reviving a being that was spiritually dead. This is a declaration of resurrection through the Guru’s grace, not self-effort, and an expression of wonder and gratitude.

Themes: Guru’s grace, naam as nectar, spiritual death and rebirth, revival of the soul, intimate address to the soul, divine gift, transformation, immortality.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਮਿਲਿ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
The divine Name (naam) is a treasure-house of amrit, deathless nectar. The exhortation is to gather in sangat, the company of the devout, and drink this nectar together. The Name is not merely recited but tasted as life-giving substance, and its reception is communal, not solitary.  
Themes: naam as nectar, treasure of the divine Name, sangat and collective worship, drinking amrit, spiritual nourishment, fellowship of the faithful
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟਿਓਨੁ ਫਿਰਿ ਜੋਨਿ ਨ ਪਾਏ ॥:
The terror of being trapped in the round of birth and death is cut away; the Divine lifts that dread and keeps the soul from returning to the wheel of becoming. It declares a state of liberation given through grace, announcing that the cycle of reincarnation is ended.

Themes: liberation from the birth-death cycle, removal of mortal fear, end of reincarnation, divine grace and rescue, release from worldly transmigration, salvation, spiritual freedom
ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਜਮ ਕਾ ਭਉ ਲਥਾ ॥੨੦॥:
Inner equipoise ripens into direct union with the Divine; once God is found, the terror of death and its messenger falls away, and spiritual death cannot approach. It declares a causal sequence: stilling the mind, meeting the Divine within, and release from mortal dread.

Themes: sahaj (natural equipoise), inner stillness, union with the Divine, finding God within, fear of death, Messenger of Death, liberation from dread, spiritual deathlessness
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਜਪਿ ॥:
Meditating on the sacred Word of the humble servant — the praise-singing utterance recited in the sangat (company of the devout) — cuts away the dread of birth and death. This is a declaration of remedy: the devotee's lifelong fear of mortality and reincarnation is sliced off by repeating the servant's Word, replacing terror with fearless trust.

Themes: fear of birth and death, cutting away dread, meditating on the sacred Word, humble servant's utterance, sangat (company of the devout), liberation from reincarnation, praise-singing, fearless trust.
ਨ ਦਨੋਤਿ ਜਸਮਰਣੇਨ ਜਨਮ ਜਰਾਧਿ ਮਰਣ ਭਇਅੰ ॥੧॥ ਰ:
Simran (loving remembrance) of the Divine is a direct remedy for human dread: birth, aging, and death no longer afflict the one who meditates. The assertion promises that heartfelt contemplation of the Divine dissolves fear, worry, and the pain of mortality. It is an assurance of fearless refuge.

Themes: simran (loving remembrance), Divine meditation, freedom from fear, birth, aging, death, existential anxiety, spiritual refuge.
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਦੁਖੁ ਕਾਟੀਐ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਚੂਕੈ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਕਾਣੇ:
The pain of birth and death is cut away within the sangat, the company of the devout, and the messenger of death loses all power to intimidate. This is a promise of liberation from the endless suffering of reincarnation and of fearlessness before mortality, grounded in love for the divine Beloved.  
Themes: sangat, liberation, birth-death cycle, fearlessness of death, end of suffering, divine Beloved, refuge.
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭੈ ਲਾਥੇ ॥੪॥੨॥੫੨॥:
The dread of repeated birth and death has been lifted; the terror of the cycle of reincarnation is dispelled. A personal testimony of release, declaring that the fear which binds one to the wheel of transmigration has fallen away, leaving a state of fearlessness and spiritual freedom.  
Themes: liberation from fear, end of reincarnation dread, release from the cycle of birth and death, spiritual freedom, overcoming existential terror, state of fearlessness.
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੈ ਆਸਰੈ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਸਿਉ ਰੰਗੁ ਲਾਏ ॥:
Relying on the shelter of the Saadh Sangat, the company of the devout, one becomes attached to the Divine and falls in love with God. The sangat is both refuge and instrument: remaining within it, a person develops heartfelt devotion and a loving bond with the Divine. This is a declarative statement of cause and effect — association with the holy is what enables the heart to turn toward God.

Themes: sangat as refuge, divine love, transformative association, devotion through community, spiritual awakening, loving attachment to God
ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗਿ ਤਰੀਜੈ ਸਾਗਰੁ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਫਾਸਾ ਜੀ:
Remaining in the sadh sangat, the company of the holy, is declared the means to cross the world-ocean and cut away death's noose. The ocean is worldly attachment and repeated rebirth; the noose is mortal fear and karmic bondage. The statement assures and urges that refuge among the devout severs death's grip and carries one to liberation.

Themes: sadh sangat, holy company, crossing the world-ocean, liberation from rebirth, severing death's noose, refuge in the devout, release from karmic bondage, overcoming mortal fear
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੀ ਭੀਰ ਜਉ ਪਾਈ ਤਉ ਨਾਨਕ ਹਰਿ ਸੰਗਿ:
Joining the throng of the holy, the sangat (company of the devout), brings direct encounter with the Divine. The statement testifies that spiritual union is not achieved alone but through the shelter and fellowship of the devout; their gathered presence becomes the meeting-place where God is found. It declares the transforming power of holy company.

Themes: sangat, holy fellowship, divine union, meeting the Divine, refuge in the devout, grace through company, spiritual transformation.
ਸੰਤਤ ਹੀ ਸਤਸੰਗਤਿ ਸੰਗ ਸੁਰੰਗ ਰਤੇ ਜਸੁ ਗਾਵਤ ਹ:
The saints remain continually joined to the sadh sangat, the company of the devout, dyed in the beautiful colour of divine love, and their whole activity is singing the praise of the Divine. A steady, blissful state of absorption in holy fellowship, not a command or plea.  
Themes: sadh sangat, divine love as dye, continuous praise, saintly immersion, spiritual transformation, blissful devotion.
ਕਾਢਿ ਲੀਏ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਆਨ ਬਿਖੈ ਤੇ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਮਨੁ ਲਾਵ:
A humble supplication asking God to pull the speaker out of vice and worldly corruption and bind the mind firmly to the sangat, the company of the devout. It casts rescue not as self-effort but as divine intervention: God extracts a person from sensory attachments and places them among the holy.  
Themes: supplication, divine rescue from vice, holy company (sangat), mind fixed on devotion, grace, release from worldly attachment.
ਮਹਿਮਾ ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗ ਕੀ ਸੁਨਹੁ ਮੇਰੇ ਮੀਤਾ ॥:
A direct address to friends, urgently summoning them to hear the greatness of the sangat (the company of the devout). It praises the holy fellowship as something glorious, a refuge of spiritual power, and insists that this glory be received with attentive listening. An invocation that exalts the collective presence of the faithful and calls the listener into receptive awe.

Themes: sangat (company of the devout), holy fellowship, praise of the sacred community, attentive listening, spiritual glory, reverence for the faithful, divine presence in collective worship
ਸੰਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਰੇਣੁਕਾ ਲੈ ਮਾਥੈ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ:
Receiving the dust of the Saints’ feet and pressing it to the forehead is an act of lowly prostration, reverence, and self-surrender. The dust is honored as the supreme gift, fulfilling every need and outweighing the nine treasures and the eighteen siddhis, the supernatural accomplishments. Contact with the holy is sought as the truest wealth.  
Themes: dust of the Saints’ feet, humility, prostration, blessing, true wealth, surrender, grace, renunciation of supernatural powers
ਗੁਰਸਿਖਾਂ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਧੂੜਿ ਦੇਹਿ ਹਮ ਪਾਪੀ ਭੀ ਗਤਿ:
Begging for grace, the speaker asks the Divine to grant the dust of the Gursikhs' feet—an image of humble contact with the holy—so that even a sinful being may attain spiritual liberation. It is a confession of unworthiness and a prayer for redemption through humility and the transforming company of the devout.

Themes: dust of the saints' feet, humility, grace of the Guru's Sikhs, confession of sin, prayer for salvation, spiritual elevation, holy company, purification.
ਕਰਉ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਭਗਤ ਜਨ ਧੂਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੩॥:
A humble prayer longs to bow before the devotees and press the dust of their feet to the face—an act of self-abasement seeking the transforming touch of holy company. It aspires to join the sangat (the company of the devout), mingle with worshippers, and sing the Divine’s praises together. The mood is reverent petition, not description.

Themes: humility, reverence for devotees, dust of saints’ feet, longing for holy company, self-surrender, collective praise
ਟਹਲ ਕਰਉ ਤੇਰੇ ਦਾਸ ਕੀ ਪਗ ਝਾਰਉ ਬਾਲ ॥:
A humble plea to remain absorbed in seva (selfless service) to the Lord's own servant, wiping his feet with one's hair as an act of bodily self-abasement and devotion. The hair, normally an adornment, becomes a rag; serving the devotee is treated as direct service to the Divine. Voiced as aspiration and surrender, not a report of a completed deed.

Themes: seva (selfless service), humility, reverence for holy feet, devotion to the Divine's servant, surrender, self-abasement, loving menial service, body as offering
ਕਰਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਧੂਰਿ ਦੇਹੁ ਸੰਤਨ ਕੀ ਸੁਖੁ ਨਾਨਕੁ ਇ:
A humble, yearning prayer: the devotee begs for divine grace in the form of the dust of the Saints’ feet, naming that sanctifying dust as the only peace desired. The stance is supplication and self-surrender, seeking holiness through contact with the devout rather than through personal merit.  
Themes: grace, humility, dust of the Saints’ feet, surrender, longing, spiritual peace, holy company (sangat), divine blessing.
ਸੰਤਹ ਚਰਣ ਹਮਾਰੋ ਮਾਥਾ ਨੈਨ ਦਰਸੁ ਤਨਿ ਧੂਰਿ ਪਰ:
A humble supplication for total bodily devotion: the speaker begs that his forehead remain pressed to the saints’ feet, his eyes stay absorbed in darshan (the blessed sight of the holy), and his body be smeared with the dust of their feet. Every sense and limb is offered for consecration through contact with the devout.
Themes: humility, surrender, reverence for the saintly, darshan, sacred dust, blessing, devotion, self-consecration
ਅਤਿ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਮਨਮੋਹਨ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਸਭਹੂ ਮਧਿ ਨਿਰਾਰੇ ॥:
Awed, adoring address to the Divine as supremely beautiful and heart-enticing, present within every being yet utterly distinct and set apart. The refrain holds intimacy and transcendence together: the Beloved pervades all existence but cannot be reduced to any created thing. The Punjabi commentary instead speaks of praise-words as spiritually life-giving, an apparent mismatch.  
Themes: divine beauty, heart-enticing Beloved, immanence and transcendence, pervading all yet distinct, awe and adoration, refrain of wonder.
ਤੇਰਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਰੂਪੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਅਤਿ ਰੰਗ ਰੂੜੋ ਮੇ:
An ecstatic outburst of praise, declaring the Divine supremely lovely in every aspect: the divine Name (naam), the visible form, and the deep hue of love (rang). It adores God not for one gift but for sheer beauty and attractiveness, celebrating that devotion itself is sweet because the Beloved is beautiful.  
Themes: divine beauty, praise and adoration, naam (divine Name), divine form, divine love (rang), wonder and bliss.
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਰਸਾਲ ਤੂ ॥੧॥:
Direct address praising the Divine as supremely beautiful and the fountainhead of all nectar-like essences. The image of nectar points to sweetness, vitality, and spiritual nourishment; beauty signals perfect, attractive form. The statement exalts the Divine as origin of every flavour and joy, declaring that all sweetness, delight, and life-giving essence flow from this one source.  
Themes: divine beauty, source of nectar, spiritual sweetness, ultimate origin, praise, divine joy, all essences, loving adoration
ਨੈਣ ਪਸੰਦੋ ਸੋਇ ਪੇਖਿ ਮੁਸਤਾਕ ਭਈ ॥:
The speaker, as a soul-bride, confesses that the Divine Beloved is lovely to her eyes; gazing on Him sends her into a state of blissful intoxication. It is a declaration of being overwhelmed, captivated, and entranced by the Beloved’s presence.

Themes: divine beauty, beholding the Divine, ecstatic love, spiritual intoxication, soul-bride devotion, captivating presence, enraptured surrender.
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਸੋਭਾ ਲਾਲ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਦਇਆਲ ਕੀ ਅਪਰ ਅਪਾਰਾ ਰ:
The lovely, radiant glory of the merciful Beloved, the Lord who sustains the universe, spreads without limit and is beautiful beyond all measure. This is pure praise and wonder, extolling a divine splendour so boundless and inexhaustible that no boundary can ever contain it.

Themes: divine glory, merciful Lord of the universe, infinite radiance, boundless splendour, awe, praise, beauty of the Beloved, limitless majesty.
ਅਪੁਨੇ ਸੇਵਕ ਕੀ ਆਪੇ ਰਾਖੈ ਆਪੇ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵੈ ॥:
The Divine personally protects the honor of those who serve Him in every circumstance and Himself turns their minds toward repeating the divine Name (naam) in loving remembrance (simran). An assurance of total divine responsibility: safeguarding and the impulse to devotion both come as grace, not self-effort.  
Themes: divine protection, preservation of honor, divine grace, naam simran, divine agency, gift of devotion, surrender, protection of devotees.
ਭਗਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਜੀਉ ਰਾਖੈ ਜੁਗਿ ਜੁਗਿ ਰਖਦਾ ਆ:
The Beloved Lord guards the honour and wellbeing of His humble devotees, and has done so consistently in every age. The statement affirms unbroken, timeless divine protection, inviting the faithful to trust in a guardianship that never fails.

Themes: divine protection, honour of devotees, timeless faithfulness, refuge in God, enduring guardianship, trust in the Lord.
ਭਗਤ ਤੇਰੇ ਸਭਿ ਪ੍ਰਾਣਪਤਿ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮ ਤੂੰ ਭਗਤਨ ਕਾ:
Addressing the Divine as Master of life and Beloved, it affirms that all devotees are dear to God and God is equally dear to them. It speaks from loving confidence, celebrating a reciprocal, intimate bond rather than petitioning or warning.

Themes: reciprocal love, divine beloved, master of life, devotees cherished by God, intimacy with God, mutual devotion, divine-human relationship
ਭਗਤਾ ਕੀ ਟੇਕ ਤੂੰ ਸੰਤਾ ਕੀ ਓਟ ਤੂੰ ਸਚਾ ਸਿਰਜਨ: The True Creator is praised as the sole support of devotees and the protective shelter of saints. The divine Name (naam) itself is that steady refuge, not any worldly prop; all security rests in the eternal Creator, voicing trust and reliance. Themes: divine support, shelter of saints, refuge in naam, reliance on God, eternal Creator, trust, protection.
ਹਰਿ ਜੁਗੁ ਜੁਗੁ ਭਗਤ ਉਪਾਇਆ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਦਾ ਆਇਆ ਰਾਮ:
The Divine Sovereign creates devotees in every age and continually comes to rescue their honor in times of distress. This praises the Lord King as a timeless protector who personally safeguards the dignity of the faithful, generation after generation.
Themes: divine sovereignty, protection of devotees, preservation of honor, timeless care, creation of the faithful, royal guardianship
ਹਮਰੇ ਕਰਮ ਨ ਬਿਚਰਹੁ ਠਾਕੁਰ ਤੁਮ੍ਹ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਹੁ ਅ:
An intimate supplication to the Divine Master: do not weigh or judge my past actions, but protect the honor (izzat) of Your own servant. The speaker appeals from strict karmic accounting to the Lord’s personal responsibility for those who surrender, asking for merciful covering, patronage, and refuge rather than just deserts.  
Themes: divine grace, forgiveness over karma, honor and shame, lord-servant bond, surrender, protection, mercy, appeal to divine responsibility
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਨਿਤ ਨਾਮੁ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਕਰੇ ਕਬੂਲੁ ॥:
A humble spiritual beggar asks for nothing but naam (the divine Name) every day, and the Lord as Master grants the request. The beggar image conveys complete dependence and lowliness, while the promise assures that sincere, persistent supplication for the Name is accepted and never refused.

Themes: supplication, humility, daily devotion, divine grace, acceptance, naam (divine Name), the Lord as Master, spiritual poverty
ਦੇਹਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਸੰਤੋਖੀਆ ਉਤਰੈ ਮਨ ਕੀ ਭੁਖ ॥:
A direct supplication pleading for naam (the divine Name) as the only true remedy for the mind’s restless craving. Receiving this gift produces santokh (contentment), so that mental hunger—the endless appetite of desire—subsides. The stance is humble petition: peace comes not by satisfying craving but by divine grace extinguishing it at the root.  
Themes: prayer for naam, contentment, ending mental craving, hunger of the mind, santokh, divine grace, freedom from desire, inner peace.
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਜਾਚੈ ॥:
A destitute seeker begs repeatedly for nothing but naam (the divine Name), addressing the Lord as the support, master, and giver of all comfort. The repeated plea is humble, urgent supplication expressing total dependence and spiritual longing rather than any request for worldly gifts.  
Themes: begging, supplication, longing for the divine Name, spiritual poverty, dependence on God, urgent devotion, yearning for naam
ਕਰਹੁ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਗੋਬਿਦੇ ਅਪਨਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵਹ:
Addressing the Divine as Gopal (nurturer of the world) and Gobind (Lord of the universe), the speaker begs for mercy not to gain worldly goods but to be helped to repeat the divine Name. Chanting naam (the divine Name) is treated as impossible without grace; the central petition pleads for divine assistance in the act of devotion itself, expressing dependence and longing.

Themes: divine mercy, grace as prerequisite, chanting the Name, naam, dependence on the Divine, supplication, prayer for spiritual capacity, loving address to the protector-nurturer
ਜਾਚਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਦੇਹਿ ਪਿਆਰਿਆ ॥:
A beggar pleads with the Beloved for the alms of the infinite divine Word/Name (Naam), not for worldly goods. The soul adopts utter dependence, making a direct, humble petition to God as a destitute seeker asking to be filled by grace. It is supplication born of longing and reliance on the Beloved’s giving.

Themes: begging, alms, humble supplication, dependence on grace, divine Name (Naam), spiritual poverty, God as Beloved, longing
ਦਰਿ ਮੰਗਤੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਦੀਜੈ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਕਰਿ:
A destitute beggar stands at the Divine threshold asking for alms, pleading that God grant mercy and bestow the gift of grace. It is a humble petition acknowledging utter dependence on the Lord's compassion rather than any personal merit.

Themes: begging at the Divine Door, divine charity, merciful grace, human helplessness, supplication, dependence on God
ਮਉਲਿਓ ਮਨੁ ਤਨੁ ਹੋਇਓ ਹਰਿਆ ਏਕ ਬੂੰਦ ਜਿਨਿ ਪਾਈ:
A single drop of divine nectar — naam, the divine Name — received into the soul makes the mind blossom and the body turn green with spiritual vitality. It declares the renewing power of even the slightest grace, picturing inner awakening as lush, living growth. One tiny drop revives the whole being, so minimal contact with the Divine brings total transformation.

Themes: divine grace, spiritual transformation, naam (the divine Name), inner blossoming, vitality, small blessing immense effect, renewal, life from water
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਤ ਸਦ ਹੀ ਰਾਤਾ ॥:
Drinking the Lord’s sublime essence—the nectar of naam (the divine Name)—keeps a person forever steeped in that color. The image of consuming divine rasa and being dyed by it proclaims continuous absorption, unbroken loving remembrance, and lasting surrender to the Divine.

Themes: divine nectar, naam (the divine Name), spiritual coloring, permanent absorption, loving remembrance, surrender, unbroken devotion
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਰਸੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਅਹਿਨਿਸਿ ਪੂਰਨ:
Exhortation to sing the Lord's praises, declaring kirtan (devotional singing) to be the ambrosial nectar that nourishes spiritual life. This divine praise is the only song worth singing; for the one who sings it, the unstruck sound current (naad) and inner instruments of spiritual bliss resonate perpetually, day and night, within the mind.
Themes: kirtan, divine praise, ambrosial nectar, naad sound current, inner spiritual bliss, continuous remembrance, spiritual sustenance.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸਨਾ ਪੀਉ ਪਿਆਰੀ ॥:
Intimate self-exhortation to the tongue, addressed as beloved: drink the amrit (immortal nectar) of naam (the divine Name). Tasting this life-giving essence means absorbing divine sweetness through speech and simran (loving remembrance), replacing worldly flavors with spiritual nourishment.  
Themes: naam, amrit, divine nectar, tongue as devotional instrument, spiritual nourishment, self-instruction, immortality.
ਤੇਰਾ ਜਨੁ ਰਾਮ ਰਸਾਇਣਿ ਮਾਤਾ ॥:
A humble servant, addressing the Divine as master, confesses being drunk on the distilled essence of the naam (divine Name). The intoxication is not worldly but a state of devotional absorption: the servant loses self-concern and remains blissfully saturated in the Lord’s presence. It is a declaration of loving surrender and spiritual ecstasy.  
Themes: divine intoxication, naam (divine Name), devotional rapture, humble surrender, simran (loving remembrance), spiritual absorption, bliss
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਆ ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦੀ ਹਮ ਨਾਮ ਵਿਟਹੁ ਕ:
Through the Guru’s Word one drinks the ambrosial nectar of Naam (the divine Name), the essence that sustains spiritual life. The speaker responds with total self-offering, declaring himself a sacrifice to that Name. It is a confession of loving surrender: the divine Word grants the life-giving taste of the Name, and the heart gives itself back in devotion.  
Themes: Naam (divine Name), Guru’s Word, ambrosial nectar, spiritual sustenance, self-sacrifice, loving surrender, devotion.
ਰਸੁ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਰਸੁ ਅਤਿ ਭਲਾ ਕਿਤੁ ਬਿਧਿ:
The ambrosial essence of the divine Name (naam) is praised as the highest, most sublime nectar, the life-giving taste that nourishes the soul. A longing question asks how this essence can be received and truly tasted by a mortal, expressing spiritual hunger for access to the supreme sweetness.

Themes: naam, ambrosial nectar, sublime essence, divine taste, spiritual longing, how to attain God, yearning for nourishment.
ਬਿਖੈ ਬਨੁ ਫੀਕਾ ਤਿਆਗਿ ਰੀ ਸਖੀਏ ਨਾਮੁ ਮਹਾ ਰਸੁ:
A loving exhortation addressed to the soul as an intimate companion: abandon the insipid, worthless water of corrupt sensory vice; drink instead the supreme nectar of naam (the divine Name). The tasteless water of worldly corruption is rejected as empty, while the divine Name is held up as sweet and satisfying, urging a decisive turn from craving to continuous spiritual absorption.  
Themes: renunciation of vice, naam as nectar, divine sweetness, worldly corruption as tasteless, spiritual discernment, intimate counsel to the soul, craving replaced by divine remembrance
ਕਬੀਰ ਬਿਰਹੁ ਭੁਯੰਗਮੁ ਮਨਿ ਬਸੈ ਮੰਤੁ ਨ ਮਾਨੈ ਕ:
The serpent of separation from the Beloved coils in the mind and cannot be charmed or driven out by any mantra. It is a confession of consuming, incurable longing: once the mind has entered the Guru's refuge, the ache of divine absence remains beyond ordinary remedies, not a sickness to be cured but a mark of love.

Themes: serpent of longing, separation from the divine, incurable ache, mind's surrender to the Guru, failure of mantras, divine love
ਹਰਿ ਬਿਨੁ ਕਿਉ ਜੀਵਾ ਮੇਰੀ ਮਾਈ ॥:
A heartbroken cry addressed to a mother as intimate witness: existence is unbearable without the divine Name (naam). The soul grows restless and anguished apart from the Supreme Soul. The rhetorical question laments that true life depends entirely on union with the Divine; severed from that sustaining presence, one cannot truly live.

Themes: separation from the Divine, longing for naam, restless anguish of the soul, total dependence on God, intimate lament, life's only source
ਪ੍ਰਭ ਮਿਲਬੇ ਕਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਮਨਿ ਲਾਗੀ ॥:
Love for meeting the Divine Beloved has taken hold in the mind, announcing an awakened longing for union with God. The heart turns inward, declaring that desire for the divine presence is now alive and active; this is a quiet recognition of devotional yearning rather than a request or plea.

Themes: longing for divine union, awakening of love, Beloved as God, transformed mind/heart, devotional desire, inward turning.
ਹਰਿ ਦਰਸਨ ਕਉ ਮੇਰਾ ਮਨੁ ਬਹੁ ਤਪਤੈ ਜਿਉ ਤ੍ਰਿਖਾ:
Addressing a companion, the speaker confesses that her mind burns with intense longing for the blessed vision (darshan) of the Divine, like a thirsty person desperate for water. The teeka names the cause as the arrow of love. This is a confession of overwhelming spiritual thirst, the soul pining for divine presence as a parched body craves water, expressing both the pain of separation and the depth of devotion.
Themes: spiritual longing, divine vision (darshan), thirst metaphor, separation from the Divine, love's wound, the mind's yearning, water as grace, desperate devotion.
ਬਾਝਹੁ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਕੋਇ ਨ ਸਾਰੇ ਏਕਲੜੀ ਕੁਰਲਾਏ ॥:
The soul, as a lonely bride separated from her divine Husband, laments that no one else asks after her welfare; she cries out unaided in the world's wilderness. It is a grief-stricken confession of total dependence: only the Beloved's caring presence can end her isolation.  
Themes: viraha (separation-pangs), divine Beloved, loneliness, world as wilderness, soul's dependence on God, lament, unanswered longing
ਮਨਿ ਬੈਰਾਗੁ ਭਇਆ ਦਰਸਨੁ ਦੇਖਣੈ ਕਾ ਚਾਉ ॥:
The mind has turned away from worldly attachment and is seized by longing to behold the divine presence. It is an inward condition of love and renunciation: a heart filled with yearning for darshan (vision of the Divine), not detached indifference but intense devotional desire. It declares the soul’s reorientation from maya (worldly attachment) toward sacred vision.  
Themes: detachment, longing for divine vision, darshan, love for the Divine, inner renunciation, yearning, turning from maya, devotional desire.
ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਚਿਰੀ ਵਿਛੁੰਨਿਆ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਬਦਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਪ੍:
A soul long separated from the Divine pleads for reunion, begging the Lord to enter the heart's inner home. The longing is bridal and intimate, addressed to God as Husband; union comes only through the Guru's Shabad, the revealed Word, which draws the Beloved to dwell within. It is a prayer of yearning, not a statement of attainment.  
Themes: separation and longing, divine union, heart as dwelling-place, Guru's Shabad as path, bride-soul and Divine Husband, prayer of return.
ਪਿਰ ਦੋਸੁ ਨਾਹੀ ਸੁਖਹ ਦਾਤੇ ਹਉ ਵਿਛੁੜੀ ਬੁਰਿਆਰ:
The soul confesses that the Divine Husband, the Giver of peace, bears no blame; estrangement is self-inflicted through her own wrongful deeds. She clears the Beloved of fault and owns her separation as personal failure, blending intimate spousal imagery with accountability.  
Themes: self-blame, accountability, separation from the Divine, divine benevolence, past misdeeds, humility, loving remorse
ਆਉ ਜੀ ਤੂ ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਹਰਿ ਜਸੁ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਸੁਨਾਵਨਾ:
An urgent, loving supplication addressed to the Guru: come, dwell in the home of my heart, and let my ears hear the Divine praises. The heart is imagined as a house receiving a longed-for guest, and hearing as the gate through which grace enters. Repeated "come" intensifies yearning and hospitality; the speaker seeks inner presence, not outer instruction.

Themes: longing for the Guru's presence, the heart as inner home, hearing divine praise, ears as gates of grace, loving supplication, holy hospitality, inner dwelling.
ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਰਾਮ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਜੀਉ ॥:
An intimate plea inviting the Beloved Divine to enter and dwell within the heart. The speaker longs for the Lord not as a distant sovereign but as a beloved presence, asking for close, indwelling union. It expresses loving yearning, devotion, and the soul’s welcome for the divine to make its home within.

Themes: divine indwelling, loving devotion, heartfelt longing, intimate relationship with God, invitation, surrender, the Beloved’s presence
ਬਿਨਵੰਤਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਦਇਆ ਧਾਰਹੁ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਨਾਹ ਪਿਆਰ:
A soul-bride begs the Divine, addressed as her Beloved Husband, to grant mercy and enter the home of her heart. The prayer is intimate and longing: she asks the absent Lord to return and abide within her inner being. It expresses bridal devotion, yearning for divine presence, and the heart as true dwelling-place.

Themes: soul-bride and Divine Husband, heartfelt plea for mercy, longing for divine presence, the heart as inner home, bridal mysticism, return and indwelling of the Beloved.
ਮੋਹਨ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਕਰਉ ਜੋਦਰੀਆ ॥:
An intimate supplication to the all-attractive, fascinating Lord, pleading with Him to come and dwell within the heart’s inner home. The voice is a yearning soul-bride who urgently invites the Beloved to take up residence, asking that the divine presence occupy the inner house as a living indwelling.  
Themes: longing for divine presence, heart as dwelling-place, intimate prayer, yearning soul-bride, invitation to the Beloved, surrender, inner temple
ਹਮ ਘਰਿ ਸਾਜਨ ਆਏ ॥:
The speaker exclaims with wonder that the Divine Friend has arrived within the heart, which is the true inner home. The Punjabi commentary reads the plural “friends” as the single Friend-Lord, now manifest in the heart-temple. The tone is joyful recognition and welcome, not request: the Beloved is already present within.  
Themes: divine arrival, heart as home, inner presence, friendship with the Divine, welcome, recognition, indwelling.
ਪਹਿਲੈ ਪਹਰੈ ਫੁਲੜਾ ਫਲੁ ਭੀ ਪਛਾ ਰਾਤਿ ॥:
Night worship in the first watch is a flower—fragrant, beautiful, full of promise—while only the final pre-dawn ambrosial watch (amrit vela) bears fruit, the mature realization. It ranks devotional timing: early-night prayer is a lovely beginning, but only practice in the amrit vela ripens into complete spiritual reward.  
Themes: amrit vela, stages of devotion, night prayer, flower and fruit imagery, spiritual ripening, promise versus fulfillment, disciplined practice.
ਕਬੀਰ ਸੂਤਾ ਕਿਆ ਕਰਹਿ ਉਠਿ ਕਿ ਨ ਜਪਹਿ ਮੁਰਾਰਿ:
Sleep is the image; the condition is maya's attachment — intoxication with worldly cares that wastes a life in unconsciousness. This is urgent self-admonition: wake from the slumber of worldly attachment, rise now, and turn to the Divine in loving remembrance (simran). Life's purpose is devotion; sleep here means forgetting the Divine, not rest.
Themes: spiritual awakening, slumber of attachment, urgent self-rebuke, loving remembrance, rejecting maya, urgency of devotion, wasted life
ਪਰਭਾਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਗੁਰ ਕੇ ਚਰਣ ਧਿਆਇ ॥:
Rise in the ambrosial hours before dawn (amrit vela), repeat the divine Name (naam), and meditate on the Guru’s feet. The feet are a humble point of refuge; fixing attention there dissolves ego and anchors the wandering mind in God. A direct instruction pairing early-morning discipline, reverent surrender, and remembrance with the Guru’s grace.
Themes: amrit vela, early morning devotion, naam simran, meditation on the Guru’s feet, humility, surrender, spiritual discipline, anchoring the mind in the divine.
ਝਾਲਾਘੇ ਉਠਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਨਿਸਿ ਬਾਸੁਰ ਆਰਾਧਿ ॥:
Rise in the ambrosial hours before dawn and repeat the divine Name; do not limit it to a morning ritual but continue in remembrance through night and day. This is instruction to the faithful, turning every hour into loving worship of the Divine.

Themes: early morning discipline, ambrosial hours, naam repetition, continuous remembrance, night-and-day worship, devotion as lifelong practice, instruction
ਬਾਬੀਹਾ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਵੇਲੈ ਬੋਲਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਦਰਿ ਸੁਣੀ ਪ:
The soul-bird, thirsting for the Divine like the rainbird thirsts for water, cries out during the ambrosial hours of the early morning. This call of deep spiritual longing reaches the Divine Court and is answered. It declares the spiritual principle that sincere prayers offered in this sacred pre-dawn time are heard by the Lord, promising the efficacy of early morning devotion.
Themes: early morning devotion, ambrosial hour, answered prayer, spiritual thirst, divine hearing, soul-bird metaphor, prayerful cry, divine response.
ਛਾਤੀ ਸੀਤਲ ਮਨੁ ਸੁਖੀ ਛੰਤ ਗੋਬਿਦ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਇ ॥:
Singing praises of the Lord of the Universe produces tangible relief: the heart grows cool and the mind settles into peace. Devotional song of divine glories cools inner turmoil and soothes the chest, a state of spiritual comfort and calm that results from praising the Divine.

Themes: cooled heart, mind at peace, singing divine praises, Gobind's glories, devotional chanting, inner relief, spiritual calm, praise as a cooling balm
ਜੋਗੁ ਬਨਿਆ ਤੇਰਾ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਈ ॥੧॥:
Singing the Divine praises is itself the attainment of Yoga—union with the Divine. Devotional kirtan (hymn-singing) becomes the true yogic practice, yielding both worldly contentment and renunciate peace. Praise is not merely preparation; the act of singing to the Divine is the realised state of union.

Themes: kirtan, divine praise, yoga as union, spiritual attainment, devotional singing, worldly and ascetic peace, surrender through song
ਹਉ ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਕਰਉ ॥:
First-person declaration of unbroken devotion: the speaker vows to fill every hour, day and night, with kirtan—sung praise—and repetition of the divine Name (naam). The image of continuous day-and-night singing conveys that loving remembrance (simran) is not occasional but the whole of one’s being and practice, a life given to worship.  
Themes: continuous devotion, kirtan, praise of the divine Name, naam simran, unceasing worship, personal commitment, loving remembrance
ਰੁਣ ਝੁਣੋ ਸਬਦੁ ਅਨਾਹਦੁ ਨਿਤ ਉਠਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਸੰਤਨ ਕ:
Rise early and join the company of the devout (sadh sangat) to sing the sweet, unbroken melody of the unstruck sound current, the divine Word itself. This is an instruction urging continuous, disciplined morning praise; it frames communal worship as a regular spiritual practice that attunes the seeker to the ever-resonant divine presence.

Themes: early morning worship, sadh sangat (company of the devout), unstruck sound current, divine Word, continuous melodic praise, disciplined devotion, spiritual practice.
ਸਾਧੋ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਕੇ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਵਉ ॥:
An urgent exhortation to the holy ones: keep singing the praises of the Lord of the universe without ceasing. Vocal praise becomes both worship and a commanded spiritual discipline, directing the mind and tongue toward the Divine and away from self. The image of singing elevates remembrance into an audible, continuous offering.  
Themes: continuous divine praise, worship through song, remembrance of the Divine, instruction to the holy, devotion as discipline
ਨਿਰਬਾਣ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਵਹੁ ਕਰਤੇ ਕਾ ਨਿਮਖ ਸਿਮਰਤ ਜ:
A direct command to become free of craving and sing the Creator’s praises from inner stillness; even a single instant of loving remembrance of the divine Name liberates from vice and bondage. It urges desireless devotional singing as a saving act.

Themes: nirvana, desirelessness, kirtan, divine praise, simran, liberation from vices, transformative remembrance.
ਮਨ ਮੀਠ ਤੁਹਾਰੋ ਕੀਓ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥:
Wholehearted surrender: the mind declares every act of the Divine sweet, accepting whatever comes as kindness. The traditional commentary makes this concrete—because of this sweetness, one never blames any person for excess or harm. It is a confession of trust and contentment, not a description of events, framing even hardship as divine sweetness.

Themes: acceptance of divine will, surrender, trust in the Divine, non-complaint, equanimity, sweetness of providence, inner contentment.
ਮੀਤ ਕੇ ਕਰਤਬ ਕੁਸਲ ਸਮਾਨਾ ॥੧॥:
Addressing the Divine as an intimate Friend, the speaker declares that every act of the Beloved is felt as comfort and ease. This is an affirmation of loving trust: divine providence, even when inscrutable, is welcomed as kindness. The heart rests in surrender, finding no displeasure in what the Friend ordains.  
Themes: divine friendship, acceptance of divine will, trust in providence, surrender, contentment, perceiving grace as comfort, loving devotion
ਸਰਬ ਸੁਖ ਆਨੰਦ ਮੰਗਲ ਰਸ ਮਾਨਿ ਗੋਬਿੰਦੈ ਆਗਿਓ ॥:
Accepting the command of Gobind (the Lord of the Universe) as sweet turns every circumstance into total peace, bliss, joy and nectar-like pleasure. This is a testimony that surrender to the divine will—hukam—brings complete inner contentment; all happiness arises from aligning personal will with God’s order, not from outward conditions.  
Themes: surrender to divine will, hukam, divine command, inner peace, spiritual joy, blissful contentment, acceptance of God’s order, Gobind.
ਖਿਨ ਮਹਿ ਥਾਪਿ ਉਥਾਪਨਹਾਰਾ ਆਪਨ ਹਾਥਿ ਮਤਾਤ ॥੧॥:
The image of all matters held in the Divine’s hands names complete authority: creation and destruction happen in a single instant by divine decree. Nothing remains fixed outside that will. The statement declares absolute sovereignty over existence, showing worldly permanence as dependent impermanence.

Themes: divine sovereignty, creation and destruction, impermanence, hukam (divine order), power over time, surrender.
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਈਐ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੧॥:
Constant contemplation of the divine Name (naam) is taught as the practice that brings every undertaking to a successful conclusion. This is both an instruction and a reassurance: fix the mind in loving remembrance of God, and all efforts, worldly or spiritual, resolve well. The repeated focus is that remembrance turns difficulty into fulfillment.  
Themes: naam (the divine Name), simran (loving remembrance), success as blessing, trust in divine timing, meditative discipline, assurance.
ਕਾਰਜੁ ਤੇਰਾ ਹੋਵੈ ਪੂਰਾ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਇ:
The mind is commanded to keep singing the praises of the Divine Name (Naam), repeating it as the one reliable work. Far from being a distraction from one’s affairs, this praise guarantees that every purpose will be fulfilled and completed. It is both an instruction to one’s own mind and a confident promise: devoted chanting bears certain fruit.  
Themes: divine praise, repetition of the Name, assured success, completion of purpose, self-instruction, fruitful devotion
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਅਰਾਧਣਾ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੮॥:
Loving remembrance of the divine Name—naam—is taught as the one practice that brings every undertaking and life’s purpose to successful completion. The teaching is prescriptive and reassuring: through simran (loving remembrance) the devotee’s worldly and spiritual affairs are resolved and fulfilled.  
Themes: naam, simran, divine remembrance, success, life’s purpose, fulfillment, resolution of affairs
ਸਭੇ ਕਾਜ ਸਵਾਰਿਐ ਜਾ ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਵੰਦਾ ॥੭॥:
All undertakings succeed not through self-effort but when they align with divine pleasure, the sole cause of their favourable resolution. Declares complete dependence: every affair is set right once the Divine looks with approval, affirming surrender to hukam (divine command) as the ground of accomplishment.  
Themes: divine will, divine pleasure, surrender, grace, success, resolution of affairs, dependence on God.
ਸਗਲ ਮਨੋਰਥ ਪੂਰਨ ਹੋਏ ਕਦੇ ਨ ਹੋਇ ਦੁਖਾਲਾ ਜੀਉ:
All worldly wants and inner longings reach total completion, leaving a state of permanent contentment where sorrow can never touch the soul. Declares the resulting spiritual condition of one established in divine connection: a condition of absolute peace, complete satisfaction, and perpetual freedom from grief. Every necessity is met; anguish is entirely removed.

Themes: fulfillment of desires, liberation from suffering, lasting peace, spiritual contentment, absence of sorrow, divine blessing, inner completeness
